title: Phosphorus Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Phosphorus Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Phosphorus deficiency shows on the old leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Phosphorus deficiency in plants starts on the old, lower leaves. Phosphorus carries energy inside the plant as part of ATP, and it is part of DNA. Young roots, shoot tips and seeds need the most, so it builds the root system and the first growth. It also drives tillering, flowering, and seed and fruit set, and it helps the crop ripen on time. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Low groundcover plant whose older leaves turn purple red, a phosphorus shortage sign

blocks.text: Phosphorus moves fairly easily inside the plant, from old leaves to new growth. So the dark or purple color shows first on the older, lower leaves, while the young leaves can look healthy.
Phosphorus deficiency symptoms

Plants grow slowly and stay short, thin and stiff, with few tillers or branches. Leaves turn a dull dark green or bluish green. Some crops show red or purple on old leaves and stems, as in corn seedlings. Flowering and maturity come late, often by a week or more, and grain, seed and fruit stay few and small. Mild cases are hard to see in the field because the plant looks green, just small.
Phosphorus deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [phosphorus in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#phosphorus).

blocks.text: What causes phosphorus deficiency

Acid upland clays in the Philippine hills lock phosphorus onto iron and aluminum, so roots cannot reach it. Volcanic, calcareous, saline and acid sulfate soils also tie it up, while sandy, eroded and degraded soils simply hold little. Cool, wet weather slows the roots, and topsoil lost to erosion takes its phosphorus with it. Every harvest also removes phosphorus, so fields fed only urea slowly run short.
How to be sure it is phosphorus

Because the leaves stay dark green, a plant short of phosphorus often passes for healthy but small. Purple corn seedlings can also come from cool weather or the hybrid itself. So compare plants of one hybrid and test the soil. A soil test for available phosphorus and pH is the best check, from a soil test kit or a DA Regional Soils Laboratory. A leaf tissue test confirms it. In lowland rice, the Minus One Element Technique (MOET) pots also show if phosphorus is the missing nutrient.
How to fix phosphorus deficiency

Work phosphorus into the soil at planting, because it hardly moves once it is in the soil. Use superphosphate (0 18 0 or 0 20 0), 16 20 0, 14 14 14 or guano. Let the soil test set the rate. On strongly acid soils, lime first, because phosphorus gives a poor return until the acidity is corrected.

How to keep phosphorus deficiency away

Return straw, manure and compost, and replace the phosphorus that each harvest carries away. Control erosion on sloping land and keep acid soils limed, so the phosphorus you apply stays where roots can use it.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: Heavy phosphorus can bring on zinc deficiency, because it ties up zinc in the soil and at the roots. Phosphorus carried off with eroded soil also pollutes the water downstream.

blocks.text: Phosphorus deficiency questions

items.q: What does phosphorus deficiency look like?
items.a: The plant stays small and thin, with dull dark green or bluish leaves and few tillers or branches. Old leaves and stems may turn red or purple, and flowering and harvest come late.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for phosphorus deficiency?
items.a: Superphosphate (0 18 0 or 0 20 0), 16 20 0 or a complete 14 14 14 worked in at planting are the usual choices. The soil test tells you how much, and very acid soils need lime first.

items.q: Why are my corn seedlings purple?
items.a: Purple lower leaves in young corn often mean phosphorus shortage, especially in cool, wet weather or on acid soil. Some hybrids are purple by nature, so get a soil test before you buy more fertilizer.

items.q: Why does my crop not respond to phosphorus on acid soil?
items.a: Acid soils lock phosphorus onto iron and aluminum, so much of what you apply never reaches the roots. Lime the field by the soil test first, then apply phosphorus so it can do its work.
